profileEvidence.author: A
profileEvidence.summary: Friendly and steady in manner, the Rabbit Dachshund retains a determined hunting spirit and a keen nose. Its smallest size traces to late nineteenth-century efforts to breed compact burrow dogs for rabbit work. Closeness to familiar people goes alongside the independent will shared by Dachshunds, whether smooth, wire-haired or long-haired.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: Friendly but independently minded, the Rabbit Dachshund carries a determined hunting spirit in the smallest size class.

sources.evidence: Pages2–5: all sizes/coats share friendly even temperament, persistent passionate hunting/excellent nose; hunting above/below ground, flushing/tracking wounded game. Pages8–9 define chest circumference measured at15months: Rabbit males27–32cm/females25–30cm; Mini males>32–37cm/females>30–35cm. Full natural tail continues topline slightly downward; feet/limbs and proportions specified. Pages5–7 define red smooth coat and wild-boar wiry coat.

sources.title: Deutscher Teckelklub1888: Rund um den Hund
sources.evidence: Organized Zwerg/Kaninchen breeding began late19thcentury selecting small burrow dogs for young fox and especially rabbits; separate size books since1980s. Character paragraphs explicitly include smallest varieties: hunting passion, intelligence/teachability, seeking human proximity, retaining independence/strong will. Legacy current-size paragraph is superseded here by FCI2022 sex-specific ranges.

sources.title: FCI: Dachshund nomenclature
sources.evidence: FCI148 lists Standard, Miniature and Rabbit, each with smooth-haired/long-haired/wire-haired subvarieties. Broad size scope is not synonymous with any single published coat leaf.
